investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-18T22:25–22:33Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state and the agent was never created.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the only 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node in the 6-node cluster could accept a new peer-pod VM at the time of the eval run. Because the pod never scheduled, the runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1859) never returned an agent, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 129s before the check timed out.
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=133618, confirming the check ran to timeout without producing any evidence.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever written, consistent with the agent never being created.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are listed as missing, matching the empty evidence object.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message, pod stuck 145s, no evidence keys — confirms the capacity problem persisted across a second independent probe attempt.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, pod stuck 146s, no evidence keys — confirms the capacity problem persisted across a third independent probe attempt spanning ~7 minutes total (22:25–22:33Z).

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all in-flight or already-running remote agent pods have claimed the available VM slots, leaving zero capacity for new scheduling requests. Preemption was also ruled out ('No preemption victims found'), meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free capacity.

[Medium confidence] The 4 nodes that do not carry kata.peerpods.io/vm are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, which is expected by design for peer-pod workloads. If the affinity/selector was recently tightened or if nodes were cordoned/drained, the effective schedulable pool may have shrunk below the minimum needed.

[Lower confidence] A node carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm may have been taken offline, cordoned, or had its resource capacity reduced (e.g., via a node configuration change or cloud provider quota reduction), reducing the pool from a previously larger set to exactly 2 eligible nodes with zero remaining capacity.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a subsequent eval run succeeds and returns vmIdPresent=true and a valid remoteState without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief spike in concurrent VM usage) rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.

If kubectl describe node output shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity was never fully consumed at the time of the failure (i.e., free slots existed), the scheduler message would need an alternative explanation such as a misconfigured resource name or a node selector mismatch unrelated to capacity.

If the 4 non-matching nodes were recently reconfigured to carry kata.peerpods.io/vm and the affinity/selector was not updated to include them, the root cause would be a selector misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes.

If a cluster-level quota or admission webhook was blocking pod creation before the scheduler evaluated node capacity, the Unschedulable message would be a secondary symptom rather than the primary cause.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly queries the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation across all cluster nodes and asserts that free capacity is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 1 free slot), providing an early warning before scheduling failures occur.

Add an eval that checks for Pending remote-agent pods older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 60s) and fails if any are found, catching slot leakage from prior eval runs or user sessions before it exhausts capacity.

Add a node-pool health eval that asserts the number of nodes matching the remote-agent node affinity/selector is at or above the expected minimum, catching unintended node pool shrinkage or cordoning.

Extend the existing remote-agent-create eval to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler event message as a named evidence field (e.g., schedulerMessage) so that future failures include structured diagnostic data rather than only a free-text check message.

This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

The pod remained Unschedulable for 146 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the pod never started, the remote agent runtime was never reachable, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was violated in full. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-18T22:25–22:33Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state and the agent was never created.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the only 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node in the 6-node cluster could accept a new peer-pod VM at the time of the eval run. Because the pod never scheduled, the runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1859) never returned an agent, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 129s before the check timed out.
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=133618, confirming the check ran to timeout without producing any evidence.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever written, consistent with the agent never being created.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are listed as missing, matching the empty evidence object.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message, pod stuck 145s, no evidence keys — confirms the capacity problem persisted across a second independent probe attempt.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, pod stuck 146s, no evidence keys — confirms the capacity problem persisted across a third independent probe attempt spanning ~7 minutes total (22:25–22:33Z).

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1851-1859: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1859; if the pod never schedules, this call cannot return an agent and no evidence can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all in-flight or already-running remote agent pods have claimed the available VM slots, leaving zero capacity for new scheduling requests. Preemption was also ruled out ('No preemption victims found'), meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free capacity.

[Medium confidence] The 4 nodes that do not carry kata.peerpods.io/vm are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, which is expected by design for peer-pod workloads. If the affinity/selector was recently tightened or if nodes were cordoned/drained, the effective schedulable pool may have shrunk below the minimum needed.

[Lower confidence] A node carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm may have been taken offline, cordoned, or had its resource capacity reduced (e.g., via a node configuration change or cloud provider quota reduction), reducing the pool from a previously larger set to exactly 2 eligible nodes with zero remaining capacity.

If kubectl describe node output shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity was never fully consumed at the time of the failure (i.e., free slots existed), the scheduler message would need an alternative explanation such as a misconfigured resource name or a node selector mismatch unrelated to capacity.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-18T22:28–22:33Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster's 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have insufficient VM capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner never received any response, leaving all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the expected-output contract entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes in the production cluster: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource report insufficient capacity (resource exhaustion), and the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. The pod remained Unschedulable for 146 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the pod never started, the remote agent runtime was never reachable, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was violated in full. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, and 4 of 6 nodes do not carry this resource or label, permanently reducing the schedulable pool to 2 nodes.
